questions.q: What is distinctive about object storage, such as AWS S3 or Azure Blob Storage?
options: It stores whole objects in a flat structure, accessed via HTTP/API calls, with no real folder hierarchy or drive mounting
It must always be mounted directly onto a single VM like a hard drive
It is only usable for real-time database transactions
It requires a fixed size to be provisioned up front, like a physical disk
questions.explain: Object storage is accessed by PUT/GET calls to a key, not mounted like a filesystem, and it scales without a fixed up-front size — great for backups, logs, and static files.

questions.q: Why is block storage, like AWS EBS or Azure Managed Disks, the right choice for a database's data files or an OS boot volume?
options: Because it offers low-latency, block-level access, behaving like a hard drive attached directly to one VM
Because it can be mounted by unlimited VMs simultaneously by default
Because it is accessed exclusively over HTTP, like object storage
Because it never needs to be formatted with a filesystem
questions.explain: Block storage is attached to a single VM and accessed at the block level, giving it the low latency a database or boot volume needs.

questions.q: What makes file storage, like AWS EFS or Azure Files, different from block storage?
options: File storage can be mounted by multiple VMs simultaneously as a shared hierarchical filesystem, while block storage is normally attached to just one VM
File storage has no real use case in cloud computing
File storage is flat with no folders, exactly like object storage
File storage cannot be accessed over a network protocol
questions.explain: File storage provides a shared, hierarchical filesystem (via NFS or SMB) that several machines can mount at once — block storage is normally attached to a single VM.

questions.q: A team needs several application servers to all read and write the same uploaded user files at the same time. Which storage type fits best?
options: Object storage, because it supports folder hierarchies
Block storage, because it can be mounted by unlimited VMs
File storage, because multiple VMs can mount the same share simultaneously
None of the three support multiple servers accessing shared data
questions.explain: File storage (like AWS EFS or Azure Files) is purpose-built for exactly this: a shared filesystem multiple VMs mount and use at the same time.

questions.q: Which storage type would be the best fit for storing database backups and log archives that are written once and rarely edited in place?
options: Block storage, because of its low latency
File storage, because it supports NFS and SMB
Object storage, because it's accessed via API and doesn't require filesystem semantics
None of the three are suitable for backups
questions.explain: Object storage's flat, API-driven, effectively infinite-scale model is a natural fit for backups, log archives, and other unstructured data that isn't edited in place.
